extra.message: Hardcoded Flask SECRET_KEY enables session/cookie forgery to escalate to admin — Attacker forges a signed session cookie granting is_admin=True and arbitrary username, bypassing login entirely and gaining full administrative access to every route that trusts session['is_admin'] or session['user']. [verified: SECRET_KEY is a hardcoded literal used by Flask/itsdangerous to sign session cookies, and session['is_admin']/session['user'] are trusted directly by routes; anyone with the key can forge an admin session.]

SQL Injection in login authentication — Full authentication bypass, login as any user including admin, potential data exfiltration via UNION-based injection [verified: Raw string interpolation of username/password into SQL at app.py:165 with special-cased handling of the OR '1'='1' bypass at 172-175; no parameterization or auth check exists.]

Insecure deserialization leading to RCE — Remote code execution on the server via a crafted pickle payload [verified: base64-decoded user data passed directly to pickle.loads at app.py:436 with no restriction, enabling RCE via crafted payloads.]

Predictable session tokens / broken authentication — Attacker who knows/guesses a victim's username can compute their session token/session_id and hijack or impersonate their session [verified: session token/session_id are deterministically derived from username (app.py:186,190) rather than cryptographically random, allowing prediction/hijack via broken_auth endpoint match at app.py:472.]

SQL Injection in comment search — Read arbitrary data from the database (users table, credentials) via UNION SELECT [verified: search_term is interpolated directly into a LIKE query at app.py:247 with no sanitization or parameterization.]

Unrestricted file upload leading to webshell execution — Upload and later access/execute a malicious script (e.g. PHP webshell) if served by an app server that executes PHP, or use as a stored-XSS/malware distribution vector [verified: Upload saves any filename (including .php) via os.path.basename with no extension/content-type allow-list, and /uploads/<filename> and /static/<path> serve it back.]

Server-Side Request Forgery in URL fetch — Access internal-only services, cloud metadata endpoints, and internal network reconnaissance from the server [verified: url form field passed directly to requests.get at app.py:384 with no allow-list, scheme, or host restriction.]

XML External Entity (XXE) injection — Local file disclosure, SSRF via external entity URIs, potential DoS via entity expansion [verified: User-supplied XML parsed via ET.fromstring at app.py:409/417 with no DTD/entity restriction; ElementTree processes DOCTYPE but has no external entity resolution in CPython by default limiting file disclosure impact, but XXE billion-laughs/DoS and some entity resolution behavior still applies depending on version — code shows no defensive parsing at all.]

SQL Injection in blind SQLi endpoint — Extract database contents via blind boolean/time-based injection [verified: user_id interpolated directly into SQL at app.py:492; IntegerField coercion doesn't prevent SQLi since form.user_id.data can still be crafted or the field itself demonstrates the vuln pattern, and no parameterized query is used.]

BOLA / IDOR on user API endpoint — Any authenticated user can enumerate and read other users' PII (email, role) via sequential IDs [verified: api_user() at app.py:608-620 fetches any user by id with only a session-presence check, no ownership/authorization check, exposing username/email/role cross-user.]

Insecure cookie flags on session cookie — Session identifier cookie readable by JavaScript (no HttpOnly) and sent over plaintext HTTP (no Secure), enabling theft via XSS or network interception [verified: response.set_cookie('vuln_session_id', predictable_session_id) at app.py:195 sets a cookie with no httponly/secure/samesite flags anywhere in the app.]

CSRF on file upload endpoint — Attacker-controlled cross-site form can upload arbitrary files to a victim's session without consent [verified: @csrf.exempt on /upload (app.py:304) removes CSRF token protection while route only relies on session cookie auth, enabling cross-site forged uploads.]

IDOR on profile endpoint — Any authenticated user can view another user's profile/account data by iterating user_id [verified: profile() at app.py:339-371 fetches and renders any user_id's row with only session-presence check, not ownership — cross-user access is the intended (and real) vulnerable behavior.]

CSRF on settings/csrf_page endpoint — Forged cross-site request can change victim's settings/state while authenticated [verified: @csrf.exempt on /csrf route (app.py:538) removes CSRF protection for a state-changing settings update relying only on session cookie.]

Missing authorization allows any authenticated user to wipe global comments data — Any low-privilege authenticated user can permanently delete all comments belonging to every user on the platform via a single POST request, causing data loss / denial of service for shared data. [verified: reset() at app.py:639 only checks 'user' in session with no ownership/role check, and for page=='comment' runs an unscoped DELETE FROM comments affecting all users' data.]

Flask debug mode enabled (Werkzeug debugger RCE exposure) — Any unhandled exception exposes the interactive Werkzeug debugger console, allowing remote code execution if the debugger PIN is bypassed or leaked [verified: app.run(debug=True) at app.py:660 exposes the Werkzeug interactive debugger on any unhandled exception, a real RCE-capable misconfiguration on a reachable path.]

Missing authentication on comments log endpoint — Unauthenticated attacker can read stored comment/log data belonging to other users without any session [verified: /comments-log (app.py:626-633) has no 'user' in session check unlike all other routes, directly serving static/comments.txt contents to unauthenticated requests.]
